title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page is not Grothendieck's own manuscript. It is page 32 of an English typescript with handwritten insertions, likely a translation of someone else's paper. The marginal 'p. 192' refers to the original pagination, and the page is also stamped '43' as archive page 43 of 61. Grothendieck evidently used the blank backs of these sheets as scrap paper: the previous page records 'faint show-through of English typescript from the other side'. The mathematics is a standard 1950s-style proof that the Euler characteristic χ(V, K(n)) of a coherent sheaf on a projective variety V is a polynomial in n of degree at most s = dim V. The proof is by induction on dimension. The opening lines finish one step: a difference of Euler characteristics is, by the induction assumption, a polynomial of degree ≤ s−1, so χ(V*, K*_n) is a polynomial of degree ≤ s. The text then sets up a comparison along a finite birational map f: V' → V, very likely normalization or desingularisation; the dictionary of the source is old-fashioned ('variety of singularities', 'biregular correspondence'). It considers the imbedding K → \bar K' = f_*(f^*K) of K into the direct image of its pullback. It also uses the base change O_{V'} → O_{V*}, giving K' = K'⊗O_{V'} → K'⊗O_{V*} = K*, and passes to direct images to get \bar K → \bar K*. With W the singular locus, U_W = V − W and U'_W = f^{-1}(U_W), the map f is an isomorphism over U_W. Hence the comparison maps are isomorphisms off W. Their kernels and cokernels are therefore supported on W, which has smaller dimension, so the induction hypothesis applies. The intended conclusion is that χ(V, K(n)) is polynomial (Hilbert–Serre).
errors: No mathematical error is visible on the page, which is a fragment of a standard argument.

The phrase 'variety of singularities' should be read as the non-normal (or singular) locus. If f is normalization, f is an isomorphism only over the normal locus, which contains the smooth locus, so the statement is fine as written.

ideas.what: Polynomiality of the Euler characteristic χ(V, K(n)) in n with degree ≤ dim V, proved by induction on dimension via a birational finite map and supports of kernels and cokernels.
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert polynomial / Snapper–Serre polynomiality of Euler characteristic
ideas.where_published: EGA III §2.5 and SGA 6 (polynomiality of Euler characteristics), though this typescript is not by Grothendieck

ideas.what: Comparison of a coherent sheaf K with f_*f^*K along a map that is an isomorphism outside the singular locus; the discrepancy is supported in lower dimension (dévissage).

deep.surprise_reason: This is the back of a sheet of someone else's typescript, apparently a translation of a 1950s paper on the Euler characteristic of coherent sheaves, which Grothendieck reused as scrap paper. It contains only standard material and nothing original to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The page is the reverse side of an English typescript (page 32 of some translation) with handwritten formulas; it is not Grothendieck's handwriting or content.
The handwritten formula reads K'⊗_{O'_V} O'_V → K'⊗_{O'_V} O_{V*}.

The repeated phrase 'the homomorphism \bar K → \bar K* and hence the homomorphism \bar K → \bar K*' is as typed; the second instance likely has a differently placed bar or star in the original (e.g. \bar K → \bar{K}^* versus \bar K → \bar{K^*}).
The last line reads K'|U'_W → (K' ⊗ O_{V*})|U'_W.
